scope: Bounded primary-source review for interpolation versus new-setting versus changed-task analogical transfer, and pre-reveal prediction commitments
execution_policy: Read-only inspection of original papers and publisher or author archives; no implementation, browser run, deployment, participant recruitment, human study, causal claim, or Gate11 work.

primary_sources.title: Schema induction and analogical transfer
primary_sources.source_type: Primary experimental paper; analogical problem transfer and schema induction
primary_sources.open_copy_provenance: Third-party-hosted copy of the original paper; the publisher DOI is the primary attribution.
claims_used: Participants read stories illustrating problems and solutions and then attempted a semantically different but structurally analogous transfer problem.
Summarization, explicit principle statements, and diagrams were experimental manipulations intended to support abstraction and transfer.
Transfer to a target should be described by the relation retained and the surface/task changes, not by novelty alone.
primary_sources.gate10_use: Predeclare whether each scored case is same-family recombination, an unseen setting preserving the task relation, or a changed-task analogical target; retain the overlap fields and score categories separately.
primary_sources.limits: The materials were verbal problem stories and a radiation problem. The experiments do not define universal near/far-transfer thresholds, validate a geometric model, or imply that a new source/query is human transfer.

primary_sources.title: Learning and Transfer: A General Role for Analogical Encoding
primary_sources.source_type: Primary experimental paper; three studies of analogical comparison and transfer
claims_used: The studies examined novices learning negotiation strategies from cases.
Comparing two cases improved abstraction and later transfer relative to studying the cases separately in the reported tasks.
The source-target relationship and the support given for comparison are part of the transfer manipulation.
primary_sources.gate10_use: Declare retained relational structure, changed surface context, and changed task demand independently; do not call a changed family transfer without recording which structure is shared and which task requirements changed.
primary_sources.limits: Negotiation cases, comparison instructions, and face-to-face transfer tasks differ from the finite 5-D point-world benchmark. The findings provide design logic, not a transferable effect estimate or proof of far transfer.

primary_sources.title: Explicitly predicting outcomes enhances learning of expectancy-violating information
primary_sources.source_type: Primary experimental paper; prediction-before-feedback versus postdiction control
claims_used: Two experiments compared an explicit numerical prediction made before the correct fact with a postdiction made after the fact was shown.
Predictions were committed before feedback and the later test was held across the prediction/postdiction comparison.
The reported memory benefit was concentrated on highly expectancy-violating outcomes.
primary_sources.gate10_use: Log an immutable pre-reveal prediction event, then reveal the answer in a separate event; preserve any correction or explanation after reveal. For a future first-exposure assessment, do not serve a protected explanation or target result to the precommit browser state before sealing. Software validation may inspect the answer key, so it verifies event ordering and served-state boundaries rather than blind human answer construction.
primary_sources.limits: The study measured human memory for numerical facts and used prediction/postdiction ordering, not geometric view prediction or analogical transfer. Its memory effect must not be extrapolated to Gate10 accuracy or agency.

derived_gate10_requirements.design: Before implementation, label every case by source family, query relation, coordinate regime, surface context, output schema, and task demand. Score same-family recombination, unseen setting, and changed-task analogical transfer separately.
derived_gate10_requirements.status: Application specification rule; not a human result.

derived_gate10_requirements.design: Seal the answer before revealing the unseen view; store commit and reveal as ordered events. Keep answer derivation independent from the hidden key and future display state; separate correction and explanation from the committed response.
derived_gate10_requirements.status: Application instrumentation rule; no prediction-learning claim without actual observations.

derived_gate10_requirements.design: Exclude practice and same-task reuse from first-exposure transfer scores. Check that protected explanation or target result is not served to the precommit browser state before sealing, and disclose that host/auditor software validation may inspect the answer key; this is not a blind human assessment. Report uncertainty by predeclared category.
basis: All three primary studies and the Gate10 scope
derived_gate10_requirements.status: Application audit rule; not directly established by one paper.

limits: No source validates the Looking Glass instrument or predicts Gate10 performance.
The studies are heterogeneous human experiments in verbal problems, negotiation, and numerical fact memory; no effect sizes are pooled or extrapolated.
Software event order, answer-key independence, and category labels can be audited without establishing human learning, transfer, calibration, or usefulness.
Novel pixels or a new source/query combination alone do not establish changed-task or analogical transfer; the retained relational structure and task demand must be specified before scoring.
